ambiguities.description: The deal says '75% of net' and 'expenses to 3550' but does not specify whether 'net' means gross minus the capped expenses (i.e., actuals capped at $3,550) or gross minus actual expenses regardless of the cap. If actual expenses run under $3,550, the result is the same; if they run over, the two readings diverge.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net = gross minus actual expenses, capped at $3,550 — artist benefits when actuals exceed the cap because the deduction is limited to $3,550.
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable when actuals exceed cap. On a $15k gross with $4,000 in actuals, artist gets 75% of $11,450 ($8,588) vs 75% of $11,000 ($8,250) — roughly $338 difference.

plausibleReadings.summary: Net = gross minus actual expenses with no ceiling — the $3,550 is a guideline or budget target, not a hard cap on deductions.
plausibleReadings.impact: Venue-favorable when actuals exceed $3,550. Same $15k gross scenario: artist gets 75% of $11,000 = $8,250 instead of $8,588.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: Can you confirm that the $3,550 expense figure is a hard cap — meaning venue expenses above that amount are the venue's responsibility and won't reduce the artist's net percentage base?

sourceText: 7,130 g'tee vs 75% of net. Expenses to 3550. Hospitality $600.
